newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick has no comment on J&H talk.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick has no comment on J&H talk.

text.p: Insurance broker Sedgwick Group Plc on Tuesday declined to comment on market talk linking it with U.S. based partnership Johnson & Higgins, one of the world's largest broking organisations.
"It's not Sedgwick's policy to comment on market rumours," a spokeswoman told Reuters.
Johnson & Higgins is considering going public or selling itself for what analysts believe could be $1.0 billion, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition.
The report said analysts believe one potential buyer could be Britain's Sedgwick Group Plc.
It also said the company has been talking to other companies about combinations, including Marsh & McLennan Cos and American International Group Inc.
J&H would make an attractive target for Marsh & McLennan, London based industry sources said.
Marsh & McLennan was toppled from its leading industry position in December when Aon Corp bought Alexander & Alexander.
In the past year, Sedgwick chief executive Sax Riley has said on several occasions that the group is looking at ways to improve its standing as a global force.
Johnson & Higgins, the third largest insurance broker in the United States, has hired Morgan Stanley & Co to explore strategic options, the report said.
